title: Export LaTeX on the Weyl Explorer (T8) and the Representation Builder (T12) writes the \dynkin line of the board, not their orbit graphs, which 6.7 says are exported as TikZ coordinates
location: site/src/components/tools/T08WeylExplorer.svelte:656 and site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:1364 (ToolFrame without latexForExport, so site/src/lib/export.ts:765-770 defaultLatexExport applies); DECISIONS.md P6-A5 request ('and if wanted T8 and T6'), answered only for T2 and T10 by P6-tikz

refute.citation: SPEC.md 6.7, last paragraph: 'Orbit graphs and projections are exported as plain TikZ coordinates.' SPEC.md 4.0 [D] Share and export: 'LaTeX export (dynkin-diagrams and TikZ, section 6.7) arrives in phase 6.' SPEC 4 T8 ('the graph of all positions reachable from all ones by legal play, drawn in layers') and T12 ('the orbit drawn in layers with edges coloured by node'). Read together, these support the finding's expected.
refute.evidence: Read SPEC 6.7 whole. The sentence has no label and no qualifier ('may', 'where ... allows'). The [S] label belongs to the compile sentence, not to this one. Section 4.0 is [D], but its LaTeX bullet points to 6.7, and 6.7 assigns orbit graphs to TikZ. Phases: T8 is phase 3, T12 is phase 5, and LaTeX export is phase 6 (4.0; 9.1 row 6 'LaTeX export'). All three are due at G6. Records at f07eec6: DECISIONS.md 'P6-A5: ToolFrame, the prop latexForExport and the default export' is a builder's design: a tool without the prop exports the board's \dynkin. 'P6-A5: TikZ export in the tools (request)' asks for T2 and T10 'and if wanted T8 and T6'. 'MERGE: P6 stage 6.1, P6-A5, and stage 6.1b, P6-A2' assigns only T2 and T10, as 'needed for the owner's G6 compile of one file of each kind'. 'MERGE: P6-tikz ...' wires T2 (tikz-graph) and T10 (tikz-points) and leaves to the owner only edge colours, labels and rise lines. No record exempts T8 or T12 from 6.7, and no section 10 default applies. The P6-A5 plan line 135 says 'T02 ... and T10 ... at least'. git grep at f07eec6 finds latexForExport passed only by T02OrbitGarden.svelte and T10GeometryStudio.svelte. reports/gate-G6.md (d59af4a, gate commit f07eec6 confirmed) checks only the three sample forms and lists no open item on T8 or T12. This is the first round of phase 6, so there is no earlier merge report. The known-and-decided list names only 'edge colours and labels in the TikZ forms'.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 6.7 states the TikZ export of orbit graphs with no permissive clause; R2 failed, because T8's and T12's figures are orbit graphs drawn in layers (SPEC 4) and 6.7 governs them; R3 failed, because LaTeX is phase 6 and the tools are phases 3 and 5, all due at G6; R4 does not apply, since no oracle value is involved; R5 failed, because the default \dynkin export is a builder's choice outside the 6.7 text, not an owner's answer or section 10 default, and MERGE scoped T2 and T10 only for the G6 compile samples without exempting the others; R6 failed, because neither gate-G6.md nor an earlier round records it. Severity stays major (a stated behaviour missing).

title: exportLaTeX writes TeX with 'undefined' and missing node names for lists that have a hole, instead of refusing
location: site/src/lib/export.ts:686-692 (edgeList: Array.prototype.every skips holes), :697-709 (tikzGraph: nodes.map skips holes), :711-729 (tikzPoints: points.map and forEach skip holes)
claim: The tikz-graph and tikz-points writers check their lists with map, every and forEach, which skip the holes of a sparse array. A hole in the vertices, the points or an edge passes every check and reaches the TeX text.
expected: exportLaTeX 'Throws RangeError, naming the fault, on data it cannot write' (export.ts:737, the CONTRACTS 4 function, plan). An explicit undefined in the same place is already a RangeError. The P6-A1 review found the same class of defect in satake.ts checkPopulation, and it was fixed with a test.
observed: tikz-points with points [[0,0], <hole>, [1,1]] and edges [[0,1]] writes '\draw (0,0) -- undefined;'. tikz-graph with edges [[<hole>, 1]] writes '\draw (nundefined) -- (n1);'. tikz-points with edge [<hole>, 1] writes '\draw undefined -- (1,1);'. tikz-graph with nodes [{x:0,y:0}, <hole>, {x:1,y:1}] writes '\draw (n0) -- (n1);' although no node n1 is defined. None of them throws. T2's and T10's adapters build dense arrays, so no reader reaches this today.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus this branch's files: npm ci; TMPDIR=<fresh dir> npx vitest run --project site-unit redteam-RT-03-p6-latex (4 of 7 tests fail).
proposedFix: Read nodes, points and each edge with index loops over 0..length-1 (or Array.from first), so a hole reaches the existing type checks.

refute.citation: decisions/P6-A5.md '2026-10-25 P6-A5: the TikZ forms': 'a coordinate that is not a finite number below 1e15 in size throws RangeError, as does an edge that does not join two given vertices or a label list of the wrong length.' CONTRACTS.md 4: 'exportLaTeX(kind, data: unknown): string; // phase 6 (P6-A5)'. SPEC.md 6.7 is silent on refusals. The recorded decision supports the finding's expected.
refute.evidence: SPEC 6.7 (read whole) says only that orbit graphs and projections 'are exported as plain TikZ coordinates'. It has no sentence that permits or forbids malformed data. CONTRACTS 4 gives only the signature, phase 6. The refusal rule is P6-A5's recorded decision, quoted above, together with export.ts:736 'Throws RangeError, naming the fault, on data it cannot write'. An edge [<hole>, 1], or an edge to a vertex that is a hole, does not 'join two given vertices', so by P6-A5's own record it must throw. Source at f07eec6: edgeList (:689) checks pairs with e.every, which skips holes; tikzGraph (:700) uses nodes.map and tikzPoints (:713, :723) uses points.map and forEach, all of which skip holes. No decision in DECISIONS.md, decisions/P6-A5.md or decisions/P6-tikz.md mentions holes or sparse lists. The same class of defect, 'a population with a hole that passes the input check', was ruled a minor and fixed in P6-A1's repair (DECISIONS.md:3520, 3708). exportLaTeX is phase 6 (CONTRACTS 4; SPEC 4.0 'LaTeX export ... arrives in phase 6'). Not in gate-G6.md. Not in the known-and-decided list (which holds only TikZ edge colours and labels). Reachability: T2's and T10's adapters build dense arrays (the finding says so), so only code reaches it.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 neither SPEC 6.7 nor CONTRACTS 4 permits writing 'undefined' or undefined node names, and P6-A5's record says such an edge throws; R2 the finding reads the docstring and the P6-A5 decision correctly; R3 exportLaTeX is phase 6 at G6; R4 no oracle value is involved; R5 no [D] or recorded decision accepts holes; R6 no record. Minor fits for an input check that only code can reach.
